title: A rejecting clause in the composed verifier
statement: Let $n>0$, let a finite-randomness nonadaptive verifier have $r$ query positions and proof length $\ell$, and let a seedwise three-CNF reduction have $K>0$ clauses per seed, be complete, and be sound. For any input $w:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, extended proof of length $\ell+K$ times the number of seeds, and seed at which the original verifier rejects using the restriction of that proof to its first $\ell$ proof bits, some clause index $q\in\{0,\ldots,K-1\}$ makes the composed three-query verifier reject on the same input and the full extended proof.
hypotheses_covered: The original verifier has a finite seed space and uses $r$ query positions
The reduction has a positive number $K$ of clauses per seed, with its stated completeness and soundness properties
The input is a Boolean word of length $n$
The extended proof has length $\ell+K$ times the number of seeds
The specified seed rejects on the input and the restriction of the extended proof to its first $\ell$ proof bits
